speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly where on your knee the pain is located and if you feel any swelling or warmth in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe how the pain feels—specifically, is it sharp and localized to the inside or outside of the knee, or does it feel like a deep ache with locking or giving way? Also, did you hear a "pop" when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints) secondary to recent increased physical activity.

REQUEST TEST: Lower Extremity X-Ray (to rule out stress fracture).
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI of the knee focusing on the medial tibial cortex and surrounding soft tissues.
